newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 5.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Constitution Drafting Assembly has approved in principle a proposal by the Constitution Drafting Committee calling for direct election of senators. The proposal was made as part of the last of the three key chapters of the draft charter which will be raised for the people to study and provide opinions before the actutal writing process begins. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Prospective buyers of stolen cars in Cambodia have opted for the more luxurious brands smuggled in from Thailand and Mercedes Benz has become the latest hit on their shopping list, says provincial governor. The brother of Agriculture Minister Chucheep Harnsawat who owns a Mercedes fell prey to a gang of car thieves yesterday. Police in Pathum Thani province say that Chucheep's silver Mercedes was stolen from a house on Monday night and that they had alerted their counterparts in Sa Kaew province, which borders Cambodia and sought their help to locate it. (THE NATION)

- Britain has called on Thailand to take immediate steps to promulgate a law against money laundering to cut off the lifeline of drug traffickers. Derek Plumby, visiting senior international drugs coordinator has expressed concern at Thailand's lack of such a law during talks with minister of the Prime Minister's Office. (BANGKOK POST)

- Problems besetting the financial sector have eased significantly as the Bank of Thailand (BOT) has given definite assurances that it will provide funding to guarantee against withdrawals from the ten finance companies which are identified as facing a liquidity crunch. Meanwhile, the ten finance firms accuse the central bank of treating them unfairly. Some of them have denied that they are in financial strife. (BUSINESS DAY) (BANGKOK POST)

- Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan will go into a crucial meeting with credit rating agency Moody's Investors Service tomorrow without details of the government's budget cuts, which failed to make it onto the Cabinet's agenda for approval yesterday. Sources say Amnuay will try to use his personal clout to convince Moody's, due in Bangkok tomorrow and Friday as part of a fact gathering mission, that the government will release details of the budget cuts in the near future. (THE NATION)

- Various large shopping centres have approached the Metropolitan Rapid Transit Authority of Thailand (MRTA) to link and develop five commercialised underground stations. However, the MRTA is negotiating the details of the proposals with the shopping centres. The proposed benefits to the MRTA could be one of the factors being considered. (THE NATION)
